Task: Explain how the browser studio chooses guest versus account drafts, saves locally and to the cloud, and prevents stale tabs or conflicting devices from silently overwriting work. Include the recovery behavior when browser storage fails. Cite the relevant source files and line numbers.

The studio uses **IndexedDB drafts keyed by `"guest"` or account UID**, with separate local and cloud conflict checks.

- **Choosing a draft.** Startup waits for Firebase authentication: signed-in users open their account draft; others load the guest draft or a blank one. A later sign-in preserves an in-progress guest draft instead of automatically replacing it. Sign-out switches back to guest after flushing local changes. [useBrowserStudioSession.ts:37–58](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L37), [220–227](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L220). The Publish panel offers “Use this device draft” or “Open my account draft.” Linking a guest draft checks for existing account work, asks before replacing it, and saves existing local/cloud versions as device recovery copies. [PublishPanel.tsx:98](components/PublishPanel.tsx#L98), [useBrowserStudioSession.ts:230–242](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L230).

- **Choosing local versus cloud account content.** Opening reads both. Local content is dirty when its timestamp differs from its last synced timestamp—or, without sync metadata, it contains work. Dirty local content with a different cloud revision triggers a choice; otherwise dirty local content or a matching-revision local copy is retained. Remaining cases hydrate cloud content, falling back to the publication or an empty account draft when no cloud draft exists. [useBrowserStudioSession.ts:84–103](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L84), [account-draft-client.ts:26–37](lib/account-draft-client.ts#L26).

- **Saving.** Edits advance `updatedAt`; local autosave is debounced 300 ms and serialized. Successful local persistence schedules dirty account sync after 800 ms. Guest drafts never enter cloud sync. Cloud saves are serialized, reuse image assets with matching hashes, upload changed images, then PUT content, asset IDs, and the expected revision. The returned sync timestamp identifies the submitted snapshot, so edits made during upload remain dirty. [useBrowserStudioSession.ts:116–131](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L116), [171–193](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L171), [210–217](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L210), [account-draft-client.ts:42–54](lib/account-draft-client.ts#L42).

- **Stale tabs and conflicting devices.** Each normal local write transaction compares the stored timestamp with the caller’s last persisted timestamp. A mismatch aborts with instructions to download the current draft and reload; deleted-account tombstones also block writes. [browser-draft.ts:30–41](lib/browser-draft.ts#L30). Cloud PUT uses a Firestore transaction that rejects a mismatched revision with HTTP 409 and increments accepted revisions. [route.ts:29–43](app/api/draft/route.ts#L29). The client responds to 409 by stopping sync, fetching the other version, and presenting an explicit choice; editing controls lock. Resolution first archives the unchosen version locally, then installs the chosen version and resumes sync. Account changes abort/invalidate old requests. [useBrowserStudioSession.ts:29](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L29), [132–168](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L132), [BrowserStudio.tsx:82–96](components/BrowserStudio.tsx#L82).

- **Failure and recovery.** Local write failure retains in-memory edits, marks saving failed, and displays the error; unloading with failed, unpersisted, or unsynced work requests a browser warning. Backup download reads current memory, including images. Recognized startup storage failure creates a blank in-memory draft and instructs enabling storage, reloading, and downloading changes before leaving. **Account-opening failure behaves differently:** it attempts a cached account draft; without one, the UI offers retry rather than a guaranteed editable fallback. Cloud retries run on reconnect and every 15 seconds unless busy or conflicted. Dirty local content plus a changed remote revision triggers a conflict. Otherwise, dirty local content or a matching cloud revision keeps the local draft; other cases hydrate the cloud draft. With no cloud draft, hydration restores the published portfolio or starts empty. Account-opening failure falls back to an available local copy and reports sync pending. ([Session:84–112](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L84), [hydration:26–37](lib/account-draft-client.ts#L26))

- **Saving.** Edits advance `updatedAt`; a 300 ms debounce queues IndexedDB persistence. Successful local persistence schedules account sync after another 800 ms. Image hashes allow unchanged uploads to be reused; the client then PUTs content, asset IDs, and its expected revision. Returned sync metadata is saved locally without replacing newer in-memory edits. Autosave writes the private draft; publication uses a separate request. ([Session:116–146](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L116), [171–213](components/useBrowserStudioSession.ts#L171), [cloud client:42–54](lib/account-draft-client.ts#L42), [publication:49–64](components/PublishPanel.tsx#L49))

- **Conflicting devices.** The server checks the expected revision inside a Firestore transaction, returns HTTP 409 on mismatch, and increments the revision only on success. The client then disables cloud saving, fetches the remote version, and presents explicit account/device choices plus downloads. Resolution first stores the unchosen version under a recovery key; choosing local content rebases it onto the fetched revision before syncing.
